paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The line chart compares the performance of two example selection strategies, ST-ES and Random, measured by minFDE₂₀ (in meters), as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linear and scaled from 0 to 15, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5, representing the count of examples used. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (m),” is linear and scaled from 16.00 to 22.00, with tick marks at regular intervals of 1.00, representing the minimum final displacement error in meters. The ST-ES line is blue with circular markers and a solid line; it starts at 22.00 at 0 examples, rapidly decreases to 16.50 at 1 example, and then gradually declines to 16.00, remaining flat from 5 to 15 examples. The Random line is orange with circular markers and a solid line; it begins at 22.00 at 0 examples, then slightly decreases to 20.90 at 1 example, and remains relatively stable around 20.70 to 20.90 for the remainder of the range, with no significant spikes or drops beyond the initial decline.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two methods, labeled “ST-ES” and “Random,” measured by the metric “minFDE₂₀ (←)” on the y-axis, which is scaled linearly from approximately 16.00 to 22.00, against the “Number of Examples” on the x-axis, which ranges from 0 to 15 in linear increments. The “ST-ES” method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 22.00 when the number of examples is 0, then sharply declines to about 16.00 by the time the number of examples reaches 15. The “Random” method is represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 22.00 when the number of examples is 0, then gradually decreases to about 20.00 and remains relatively stable thereafter, fluctuating slightly between approximately 20.00 and 20.50 for the remainder of the x-axis range.
